evidence.verification: `cd research/categorical-scores && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 6 tests OK, 0.70 s. Tests check closed forms against direct enumeration, vertex worst case against random search, curvature against finite differences, sqrt(K). quality_mutate.py: 2 of 4 seeded mutants caught (curv_log 2*a -> 2.01*a caught; max_regret_spherical min(p) -> 0.999*min(p) caught), 2 survived: kl returning 0 instead of inf for a zero report, and log_loss returning 0 for r_y=0 (which makes log improper). Both zero-probability branches are exactly what the paper's 'log is not blind to a dropped class' claim rests on, and no test touches them.
evidence.craft: Read src/categorical_scores/model.py (92 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py. Clean, stdlib only, closed forms documented with their derivation in docstrings, figure parses numbers from results.txt instead of retyping. Defects: no validation that a report lies on the simplex (negative entries or sum != 1 silently give meaningless regrets); spherical_loss and spherical_regret divide by zero on a zero vector; `from .model import *` package API. Acceptable for a research module.
evidence.claims: Checked: worst-case formulas (backed, tests + my grid); 'spherical beats Brier by exactly sqrt(K) at uniform' (backed, E3 + my FD); 'worst regret 0.25-0.5 of range vs 0.40-0.62' (backed: 0.247..0.4985 vs 0.400..0.624); 'ratio 1.4-2.2' in sec. 3 (backed, E2 1.386-2.236). Not backed: whitepaper.md:18 'spherical at 1.75-2.2' for every rho contradicts E2 (1.386 at rho=0.5); whitepaper.md:15 'verified against finite differences to 0.1%' but the test tolerance is 0.5% (assertAlmostEqual places=2 on the ratio) and at the test's own seed the spherical error reaches 0.31%; whitepaper.md:18 log loss 0.151 'for zeroing out a class' is a floor artefact. The paper does say 'not new theory', which is honest. No references to prior work at all.
evidence.fitness: Nearest prior work: Bickel (2007, Decision Analysis) compares exactly the quadratic, spherical and log rules, including on rare outcomes; Gneiting & Raftery (2007) give the regret/divergence forms (Bregman for Brier, KL for log); Friedman (1983) and Li, Hartline et al. (EC 2022) normalise scores to a bounded range to compare incentives. The paper cites none, only sibling repo projects. New relative to these: the explicit spherical curvature ||delta_perp||^2/(2||p||) and the exact sqrt(K) range-normalised ratio at uniform truth, which are short derivations. Sound, and a researcher could reuse the module, but as a contribution it is a technical note, not a paper; the motivating use (verifier payments with stake coverage) is not exercised.
evidence.domain: Methods agree with the standard (Gneiting & Raftery 2007 properness; Brier regret = squared Euclidean distance; log regret = KL; spherical regret = ||p||(1-cos theta)); quasi-concavity argument for the spherical vertex minimum is correct. Departures a referee would raise: the 'per unit of payment range' normalisation is asserted, not argued (Brier's range 2 is only reachable at opposite vertices, and a range-of-expected-score or per-unit-of-expected-payment normalisation, which the limits mention, can reverse rankings); the rare-class comparison uses one arbitrary floor; no literature review; no empirical forecasts or scoring-rule sensitivity analysis of the kind Bickel or Merkle & Steyvers (2013) provide.

E4 log regret 0.151 at rho=0.01 is presented as the loss for 'zeroing out' a class but depends on the arbitrary 1e-9 floor (0.082 at 1e-6, infinite at a true zero)
'spherical at 1.75-2.2' per range for every rho contradicts E2 (1.386 at rho=0.5)

verdict: A small, correct technical note. Every number I recomputed from textbook definitions matches: properness holds numerically, the vertex worst-case regret formulas equal a brute-force grid maximum, and all E1-E3 values and the E4 Brier values reproduce exactly (E2 to 3 dp under 60-digit finite differences). It does not meet the bar: claims=2 (three text claims are wrong or overstated, including a log 'drop-a-class' loss that is a 1e-9-floor artefact), verification=2 (2 of 4 seeded mutants in the zero-probability branches survive), and fitness/domain=2 because the paper cites no prior work (Bickel 2007 compares exactly these three rules) and its range-normalisation convention is asserted rather than argued.
